canonical.name: The projection of a smooth vector bundle is locally the product projection and hence a surjective submersion
A supplied countable GL(r)-cocycle yields a Hausdorff second-countable smooth vector bundle, and gauge-equivalent cocycles give isomorphic bundles
Vector bundle chart changes are fibrewise linear with smooth GL(r)-valued transition functions on overlaps
Vector bundle transition functions satisfy the identity and cocycle laws on overlaps
Restricting a vector bundle to an open subset keeps the same fibres over the smaller base
The zero section is locally a coordinate slice and the total space has the expected local dimension
A local frame is a pointwise basis of sections on an open set, and a global frame is such a basis on all of the base
A local frame defines a trivialization and conversely, with the change-of-frame matrix governing the bundle transition law
Smooth sections are exactly smooth local coordinate tuples, and locally finite section sums remain smooth
Bundle maps are read off from smooth local matrices, and fibrewise invertibility over a diffeomorphism gives a smooth inverse
In local frames, a bundle map is smooth exactly when its matrix coefficients are smooth scalar functions
Constant-rank kernel and image constructions are smooth only after fixing a locally nonzero minor
The pullback bundle is the fibre product {(q,e) : f(q) = pi(e)} over the new base
The pullback bundle uses paired base-fibre data and is not the old total space viewed over the new base
Pullback is functorial up to the canonical id^*E ≅ E and (f∘g)^*E ≅ g^*f^*E bundle isomorphisms
The Whitney sum is the fibrewise direct sum of two vector bundles over a common base
Whitney sums inherit smooth bundle structure from block-diagonal transition functions
Whitney sums use block-diagonal transitions, while dual and Hom bundles use inverse-transpose and conjugation formulas
Sections of Hom(E,F) and sections of Hom(E,f^*F) encode bundle maps over the identity and over an arbitrary base map
The quotient bundle by a subbundle is defined fibrewise and later shown to have an atlas independent of adapted frames
Adapted local frames produce quotient bundle charts and the canonical quotient bundle map
The canonical projection to a quotient bundle is a smooth bundle map with kernel equal to the chosen subbundle
A smooth bundle metric is a fibrewise positive-definite inner product varying smoothly in local trivializations
Partition-of-unity averages of local Euclidean metrics stay positive definite fibrewise
A smooth bundle metric and smooth Gram-Schmidt produce smooth orthogonal complements of subbundles
Every vector subbundle has a smooth complement after choosing a bundle metric
Smooth Gram-Schmidt turns an adapted frame into an orthogonal splitting and yields noncanonical bundle complements
The intrinsic normal quotient TM|_S/TS and conormal annihilator N^*S define the normal and conormal bundles of an embedded submanifold
The intrinsic normal quotient and the conormal annihilator are smooth local coordinate quotients and subspace bundles
A chosen ambient metric identifies the normal quotient with an orthogonal normal subbundle, but only after that choice
At a zero of a section, the derivative of the local component map controls the vertical differential because the frame-change correction vanishes at zero
Vector bundles need not be globally trivial
Fibrewise linearity and continuity do not force smoothness of a bundle map
Fibrewise quotients by arbitrary varying subspaces need not form a smooth vector bundle
A short exact sequence of vector bundles need not split canonically
Orthogonal normal bundles depend on a metric even though normal quotients are intrinsic
A pullback bundle is fibre-product data, not the set-theoretic inverse image of the old total space
The Mobius line bundle arises from the sign transition function on the circle
The tautological line bundle on real projective space has explicit local frames and transition functions
The sphere's normal bundle is trivialized by the outward radial field
A nowhere-zero tangent field trivializes the tangent bundle of the circle
The hairy-ball obstruction is recorded as a later consequence rather than proved on this page
Pulling back the tautological line bundle along the antipodal cover produces a trivial bundle with an explicit nowhere-zero section
The graph of a bundle map is a vector subbundle of the corresponding Whitney sum
A rank-jumping kernel fails to be a vector subbundle
